issue.title: Build the per-year ranking screen with drag and drop and covers
issue.body:
A page for one year where the user builds a ranked top 10, honorable mentions and a list of albums they heard but did not place, by dragging album covers, replacing the "Ranked" sheet. Needs catalog search (#5) and the data model (#4). Part of the MVP defined in #2.

## Today
No code exists. In the spreadsheet a year is a row of text: ranks 1 to 10 in order, then an unordered honorable mention list, and in many early years albums with neither (81 rows, mostly 1960 to 1981). Years can have fewer than 10 ranked albums.

## Scope
- A year page (pick any year) with three areas:
  - ten ordered rank slots with cover art,
  - an unordered honorable mention area,
  - an unordered **listed** area for albums heard that year but not placed.
- Add an album from catalog search into any area.
- Reorder by drag and drop, move between a rank slot, honorable mentions and listed, and remove. Changes save to storage.
- Show each album's current rating next to it, from the Elo engine (#7). Listed albums have no rating.
- One album, one year: adding an album that is already on another year page asks to move it.
- Create a manual album (title, artist, year) when the catalog does not have it, shown with the placeholder cover.
- Keyboard-usable reordering and touch drag, so it works without a mouse.
- Empty states for a year with no albums and for a year with fewer than 10 ranked.

## Acceptance
- Dragging an album from rank 4 to rank 1 shifts the others down by one and the order survives a page reload.
- Adding an album already on another year asks to move it, and moving it removes it from the first year.
- A year with 3 ranked albums renders with 7 empty slots and saves.
- Component or end-to-end tests cover add, reorder, move between the three areas and remove.

## Out of scope
- Computing the ratings (the Elo engine ticket).
- Artist and decade views.
- Importing the spreadsheet.

issue.title: Build the Elo rating engine and matchup screen
issue.body:
A rating engine that turns year placements and head-to-head answers into one Elo rating per album, plus the matchup screen where the user answers "which of these two do you like more?". One algorithm, no settings. Needs the data model (#4). Part of the MVP defined in #2; the scoring rules are in the spec's § Scoring.

## Today
No code exists. The spreadsheet's points table, honorable mention value and year weight are not carried over: the spec replaces them with Elo.

## Scope
- **Rating engine.** Pure functions, no UI. Ratings are computed by replay, never stored:
  - Standard Elo: every album starts at 1500, `expected_A = 1 / (1 + 10 ^ ((rating_B - rating_A) / 400))`, `rating_A += K × (score_A - expected_A)` with score 1, 0.5 or 0, and B moves by the same amount the other way. `K = 32`. The constants are fixed in code.
  - Only albums with a ranked or honorable mention placement are rated. Listed albums have no rating.
  - Seeding from year placements: within a year each ranked album beats every album ranked below it and every honorable mention. Honorable mentions do not play each other. Implied results are derived on every replay, not stored.
  - Replay order: implied results first, year by year ascending, higher ranks first; then explicit matchup answers, oldest first.
- **Artist score** as a function: `(sum of ratings + 1500) / (album count + 1)` over the artist's rated albums. The per-decade version uses only albums placed in that decade.
- **Matchup picking:** only albums from different years, never a listed album. Pick the rated album with the fewest explicit matchups (random among ties), then the opponent from another year with the closest rating, skipping a pair already played.
- **Matchup screen:** two album covers side by side. The user picks one, calls a tie, or skips. A skip records nothing and serves the next pair. Undo deletes the last answer. Each answer updates the ratings straight away. A counter shows matchups played.

## Acceptance
- Two new albums at 1500, A wins: A is 1516, B is 1484. A tie between 1500 and 1500 changes nothing. Replaying the same inputs twice gives the same ratings.
- On a fixture year with no explicit matchups, the replay plays exactly the implied results: ranked over lower ranked, ranked over honorable mention, nothing else.
- Answering a matchup changes both ratings. Undo restores the previous ratings exactly.
- The screen never serves two albums from the same year, a listed album, or a pair already played while an unplayed pair exists.
- An artist with albums rated 1600 and 1700 has a score of (1600 + 1700 + 1500) / 3 = 1600.
- Unit tests cover each function with fixed inputs; the screen is covered by a component or end-to-end test.

## Out of scope
- Other scoring algorithms, a settings screen, points tables or year weights.
- Artist and decade pages that show the results (#8, #9).
- Importing the spreadsheet.

issue.title: Add decade top 25 album lists
issue.body:
Per-decade lists of the 25 best albums, hand-ranked as in the spreadsheet, with covers and a rating-based suggestion for decades that have no list yet. Replaces the "Decade Top 25" columns and the By Decade sheet. Related: #8. Needs the Elo rating engine (#7). Part of the MVP defined in #2.

## Today
No code exists. In the spreadsheet 75 albums carry a decade rank, typed by hand: 25 each for the 1960s, 2000s and 2010s. The candidate flag is not used consistently, so it is not carried over.

## Scope
- A decade page listing the top 25 albums with cover, position, artist, year and rating.
- The list is hand-ranked. Any album with a ranked or honorable mention placement in that decade can go on it; the decade is the album's year page decade, not its catalog release year. There is no candidate flag.
- Add albums to the list and reorder by drag and drop, up to 25 per decade. Store each entry in the data model's decade list entry (#4).
- A decade with no list shows a suggestion: its top 25 albums by rating. The user can accept it and then reorder. A suggestion is not saved until accepted.
- Decade picker for every decade that has albums.

## Acceptance
- A decade with fewer than 25 eligible albums renders what it has.
- Reordering persists across reload, and a 26th album is refused.
- An empty decade shows the rating-based suggestion, and nothing is saved until the user accepts it.
- Tests cover list building and the suggestion for a decade.

## Out of scope
- Artist views (#8).
- Importing existing decade ranks (the import ticket).

issue.title: Import the existing spreadsheet
issue.body:
Load the user's `Best Albums.xlsx` into the app, so years of rankings are not retyped. Related: #5. Needs the data model (#4) and catalog search (#5). Part of the MVP defined in #2.

## Today
No code exists. The file is the user's and is not in the repo. Its Albums sheet has 752 album rows, years 1955 to 2024, with columns for rank, album, artist, year, honorable mention flag, decade top 25 candidate flag, decade top 25 rank and the derived scores. The rows are:

- 292 ranked (rank 1 to 10),
- 378 honorable mention,
- 1 ranked and flagged honorable mention (a 2014 row, rank 5),
- 81 listed only (no rank, no honorable mention), mostly 1960 to 1981.

One pair (a 1960 album) is an exact duplicate row. 75 rows carry a decade rank.

## Scope
- A command-line script, run once with the file path. It reads the Albums sheet's input columns (album, artist, year, rank, honorable mention, decade top 25 rank) and creates year entries and decade list entries. It ignores the derived columns, `New`, the candidate flag and the pivot sheets.
- Row mapping: rank becomes ranked; the honorable mention flag becomes honorable mention; neither becomes listed. The flag wins over a rank, as in the sheet, and that row goes to the review page.
- Match each row to a catalog album using catalog search (#5). Auto-accept clear matches. Send ambiguous or missing ones to a review page in the app, which the import fills. There the user picks a match or keeps the row as a manual album.
- Merge exact duplicate rows (same album, same year) into one entry and list them in the summary.
- Safe to re-run: an entry already imported is not added again.
- A summary at the end: rows read, matched, sent to review, merged, skipped.
- Do not commit the spreadsheet, rows from it or any personal data. Test fixtures use made-up rows.

## Acceptance
- After importing the user's file and resolving the review page, every year page shows the sheet's ranks, honorable mentions and listed albums for that year, and the 1960s, 2000s and 2010s decade lists match the sheet's decade ranks. The only differences are the merged duplicate and the rank-plus-honorable-mention row, both named in the summary.
- A second import changes nothing.
- A row with a typo in the title lands in the review page, not the data.
- Tests use a small fixture file of made-up rows covering each row kind, a duplicate and a rank-plus-honorable-mention row.

## Out of scope
- Importing the artist rollup sheets (recomputed by the app).
- Importing the spreadsheet's weighted scores. The app does not use them.
- Exporting back to a spreadsheet.

issue.title: Epic: Album ranker MVP
issue.body:
Replace the "Best Albums" spreadsheet with an app where the user searches an album catalog, ranks favorites per year with cover art, and gets artist and decade lists from Elo ratings built from yearly ranks and head-to-head matchups. The requirements are settled in #2; the other tickets build what it describes.

This epic is a container. The team builds its child tickets, not the epic itself.

## Tickets

* #2 Write the MVP requirements spec for the album ranking app (first; the build tickets follow it)
* #3 Choose the tech stack and scaffold the app
* #4 Define the data model and storage for albums, years and rankings
* #5 Add album catalog search with cover art
* #6 Build the per-year ranking screen with drag and drop and covers
* #7 Build the Elo rating engine and matchup screen
* #8 Add artist views by decade and overall
* #9 Add decade top 25 album lists
* #10 Import the existing spreadsheet
* #14 Deploy the app to AWS with staging and production behind a password gate

issue.title: docs: ALBUM-2 MVP requirements spec
issue.body:
## Summary

Adds the MVP requirements spec for the album ranker: one-person web app, SQLite, catalog search with covers, per-year ranking screen, head-to-head Elo ratings (single algorithm, seeded from the yearly ranks), artist and decade views, and a one-off spreadsheet import. The spec also records what the real `Best Albums.xlsx` formulas say, which differs from the ticket's description (752 rows, 81 listed-only rows, the year weight formula, two artist rollup rules).

Ticket: ALBUM-2 (https://github.com/dbeallor/album-ranker/issues/2)
Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-album-ranker-mvp.md`

Closes #2

## Changes

- New spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-album-ranker-mvp.md`. No code.

Context size: pass skipped (not collective-wisdom)

## Proof

- **Spec committed and approved**: spec is on this branch. The user approved it in the Chief of Staff thread ("approve 2") after the Elo revision at commit 3091b45.
  After that approval, code review fixes amended the spec (rules the approved version left undefined, no change of direction): replay tiebreaks, skipped matchups, decade list upkeep, import conflict and re-run rules, the rank-plus-honorable-mention row imported as an honorable mention without a review item, and listed albums showing no rating. The merge approval covers them.
- **Every Scope item has an answer or an open question**: users and shape (§ Users and shape), MVP features, scoring (§ Scoring: head-to-head Elo), decade top 25, albums versus releases, data model outline, non-goals, calls I made, and whole-MVP acceptance each have a section; unresolved items are in § Open questions for the user.

Not proven:
- Follow-up tickets #3 to #10 still match the spec: a ticket child may only change its own ticket, so the spec's § Follow-up tickets: changes needed lists the edits for the Chief of Staff or the user to apply.

issue.title: feat: ALBUM-4 data model and storage
issue.body:
Closes #4

Ticket: [ALBUM-4](https://github.com/dbeallor/album-ranker/issues/4). Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-21-album-4-data-model-storage.md`. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-21-album-4-data-model-storage.md`.

## What this adds

- SQLite storage on Node's built-in `node:sqlite`, no new dependency and no ORM.
- Numbered SQL migrations (`lib/db/migrations/001_initial.sql`) with a runner, applied on first open or with `npm run db:migrate`.
- Six tables: artists, albums, year entries, matchups, decade list entries, import review items. Only inputs are stored.
- A data access layer in `lib/db/` that enforces the spec's rules (one year entry per album, unique ranks, rank matches placement, decade list eligibility and follow-along removal, undo, cascade deletes, manual album linking).
- README step for `npm run db:migrate`.

No screens or routes.

## Proof

- **Year entry CRUD, second entry and duplicate rank rejected**: `lib/db/year-entries.test.ts` passes.

  ```
  $ npm test
   Test Files  10 passed (10)
        Tests  73 passed (73) (37 of them ALBUM-4; the rest came from main)
  ```

- **Three placements, manual album linking, matchup insert and undo, decade list rules**: `albums.test.ts`, `year-entries.test.ts`, `matchups.test.ts`, `decade-lists.test.ts` in the same run.
- **Schema setup from a clean checkout**: `npm run db:migrate` with `DATABASE_PATH` in a temp folder created the folder and file, and a second run did nothing.

  ```
  $ DATABASE_PATH=$TMP/x/t.db npm run db:migrate
  Database ready at $TMP/x/t.db
  ```

- **Lint, typecheck, build**: `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` print no errors; `npm run build` succeeds.

Not proven:
- CI: the repo has no CI yet.
- The `server-only` import in `lib/db/server.ts` under a real route: nothing imports it yet.
